title: AML alert triage (VAOM v5 worked example 7B)
description: Alert triage at a mid-sized European bank: about 800 alerts a day, roughly 95% false positives. Figures the whitepaper states are used as stated; figures it doesn't state (calibration samples, the lower confidence threshold, review times, funded hours) are illustrative and say so in each row.

no-sar-filing-tool.description: No capability to file a suspicious activity report is mounted for the agent, and its credentials carry no filing scope.

verification.probe: Attempt a SAR submission from inside the agent context.

rows.title: Dismiss an alert outside the typologies
rows.description: The narrow delegated slice of a regulated decision: dismissing alerts that deterministic checks confirm fall outside the typologies altogether (own-account transfers, salary payments matching employer records, utility payments within historical range). The thresholds' upper value 0.95 follows the paper (composites above 0.95 reach Band A; 0.83 reaches review); the lower value 0.70, the calibration record, review and audit times are illustrative.

restrictions.reason: No alert involving a politically exposed person may be auto-dismissed.
No alert involving a sanctioned jurisdiction may be auto-dismissed.

regulatedJustification.retainedByHuman: The regulated determination itself, whether the activity is suspicious and whether a SAR must be filed, stays non-delegable (row sar.determine) under Prepare & Present.
regulatedJustification.whyNarrower: Only alerts that deterministic checks confirm fall outside the typologies altogether are dismissed. That narrows regulatory exposure rather than expanding it, and a dismissed alert can be reopened and re-triaged.
regulatedJustification.bounds: Hard non-delegable overrides for politically exposed persons, sanctioned jurisdictions and amounts over the reporting threshold (the ceiling), whatever the score; independent verification required for Band A; a 10% weekly audit of auto-dismissals.

rows.title: Determine suspicion and file a SAR
rows.description: Whether activity is suspicious and whether a SAR must be filed: the MLRO's determination. The agent assembles the investigation package (row alert.prepare) and never files.

authority.reason: A regulated determination that law reserves to a human: suspicion and SAR filing.

rows.title: Assemble the investigation package
rows.description: Reading the alert, the account profile and transaction history, and drafting the package an investigator or the MLRO decides on.
